blocks.text: 1. Word2Vec

blocks.alt: A text corpus goes through Word2Vec to produce word vectors

blocks.text: Word Embeddings, the previous topic, introduced dense, meaningful vector representations for words. Word2Vec is one of the earliest, most influential techniques for actually learning these embeddings, explored throughout this topic.
It is a genuinely simple, elegant neural network trained specifically to produce dense word vectors, a genuinely landmark technique covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Foundational Insight
This connects back to learned from co-occurrence, already covered in Word Embeddings. Words that genuinely appear near each other often genuinely share related meaning, already covered there.
Word2Vec is genuinely the concrete, working technique built directly around that foundational insight, turning that earlier linguistic observation into a genuinely working, trainable neural network.
3. The Core Idea

blocks.alt: A word and its context predict each other

blocks.text: Word2Vec's genuinely core idea connects back to self-supervised objectives, already covered in Pretraining. Train a genuinely simple network to predict context from a word, or a word from its context.
This directly reuses the self-supervised philosophy already covered there, needing genuinely no separate, human-labeled data at all, just raw, genuinely available text.

blocks.text: 4. Two Word2Vec Architectures

This connects back to the core idea, already covered in this topic. Word2Vec genuinely comes in two variants: CBOW and Skip-gram, both directly implementing the same core idea in two genuinely different directions.
Both are covered in complete, dedicated depth in the next two topics of this module, exploring exactly how each variant genuinely differs in its own specific prediction direction.
5. A Genuinely Shallow Architecture

blocks.alt: An input layer feeds a hidden layer, then an output layer

blocks.text: This connects back to Network Architecture, already covered in its own topic. Word2Vec genuinely uses a genuinely shallow network, just one hidden layer, a deliberately simple design.

This is a genuinely deliberate design choice keeping training genuinely fast even at genuinely large vocabulary scale, prioritizing genuine efficiency over the genuinely deeper architectures already covered elsewhere in this course.
6. The Hidden Layer Becomes The Embedding

blocks.alt: Hidden layer weights become the word embedding

blocks.text: A genuinely elegant, distinctive insight connects back to the hidden state, already covered in its own topic. After training, the genuinely hidden layer's own weights themselves become the genuinely final word embeddings.

This genuinely elegant insight, already covered in this section, means Word2Vec's own genuinely simple prediction task is really just a clever, indirect way of training genuinely useful embeddings as a genuine byproduct.

blocks.content: This genuinely elegant insight, already covered in this topic, is exactly why Word2Vec's own prediction task, already covered as the core idea, is genuinely secondary; the real, valuable output is the learned hidden layer weights themselves.

blocks.text: 7. A Preview Of Negative Sampling

blocks.alt: All vocabulary words are compared against a few negative samples

blocks.text: This connects back to Softmax's own computational cost over large vocabularies, already covered generally in the Activation Functions module. A genuinely practical technique, negative sampling, genuinely speeds up training over genuinely enormous vocabularies.

This avoids the genuinely full, expensive Softmax computation at every single training step, a genuinely important, real practical optimization explored further as this technique matures throughout practice.
8. A Genuine Historical Contribution

A genuinely important historical contribution connects back to AlexNet, already covered in the CNN Architectures module. Word2Vec genuinely demonstrated that neural networks could learn genuinely rich, meaningful word representations at genuinely large scale.

This directly parallels AlexNet's own genuinely dramatic demonstration already covered there, just applied to genuinely textual data rather than images, helping launch the broader use of learned embeddings throughout natural language processing.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why Word2Vec Is Genuinely Still Worth Understanding

blocks.alt: Needing efficient word vectors points toward considering Word2Vec

blocks.text: This connects back to CBOW and Skip-gram, covered in the next two topics of this module. This exact technique, already covered in this topic, directly underlies both of those genuinely important variants.

Wanting genuinely efficient, fast-to-train word embeddings for a genuinely large vocabulary is another genuine case where Word2Vec's own shallow architecture, already covered, directly delivers exactly that.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates Word2Vec's own conceptual training setup, extracting context windows from a sentence, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
sentence = ["the", "quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps", "over", "the", "lazy", "dog"]
window_size = 2  # already covered as the context window in this topic

training_pairs = []
for i, target_word in enumerate(sentence):
    context_start = max(0, i - window_size)
    context_end = min(len(sentence), i + window_size + 1)
    context_words = [sentence[j] for j in range(context_start, context_end) if j != i]
    training_pairs.append((target_word, context_words))

print("Word2Vec training pairs (already covered as the core idea in this topic):")
for target, context in training_pairs[:4]:
    print(f"  Target: '{target}', Context: {context}")

print(f"\nTotal training pairs generated: {len(training_pairs)}")
print("Each pair, already covered in this topic, teaches the network to associate a word with its own surrounding context")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Word2Vec is a simple, elegant neural network trained specifically to produce dense word vectors.
It turns the foundational co-occurrence insight into a concrete, trainable network.
It trains to predict context from a word, or a word from its context.
It comes in two variants, CBOW and Skip-gram, covered in the next two topics.
It uses a genuinely shallow architecture, just one hidden layer, for fast training.
The hidden layer's weights themselves become the final word embeddings.
Negative sampling speeds up training over enormous vocabularies, avoiding full Softmax computation.
It demonstrated that neural networks could learn rich word representations at large scale.
Next up: CBOW, a complete, dedicated look at Word2Vec's first variant.
